items.summary: Reproducible report: a blocking call (time.sleep(60)) inside an async handler is not interrupted by call_timeout=1, so the whole worker stalls for 60 seconds. This is likely because a synchronous blocking call in the event loop cannot be cancelled by an asyncio-based timeout. Fix options include running blocking tools in an executor or documenting the limitation. It already has needs-review.
missing_information: Which version of the project/library is affected?
Is the timeout implemented with asyncio.wait_for or something else?
Is running blocking tools in a thread/executor an acceptable fix, or should this be documented as unsupported?

issues.title: Worker hangs on a blocking tool
issues.body: Python 3.12, Ubuntu. An async action calls time.sleep(60). The configured call_timeout=1 does not interrupt it. Reproduction: put time.sleep(60) inside the async handler. Expected: worker remains responsive. Observed: all tasks pause for 60 seconds.
